_what: The win model's constants. A forecast for games not yet played, from the
NCAA's NET and the AP poll, and nothing else: no injuries, no travel, no
who is suspended, no who played last night. It is a starting point for an
argument, not an answer, and the app says so beside every number it shows.
z is team strength in standard deviations above an average Division I
team, worked out from a team's NET rank by the Blom transform:
A rank has to be transformed because it is ordinal - 1st to 10th is a far
bigger step in strength than 200th to 210th - and the NCAA publishes no
rating behind it. Its own FAQ says the NET's components are machine-learned
with 'no static formula', so there is nothing to read off. The transform is
not arbitrary: the NCAA states a 90th-percentile team sits around NET 36,
and Blom puts rank 36 at the 90.2nd percentile of 363 teams.
_where_the_numbers_come_from: Both fitted to the 2025-26 final NET file in scraped/, not borrowed.
homeAdjustment: across all 363 Division I teams, home records summed to
3028-2029, a 59.9% home win rate. That is unbiased however the schedule
fell, because every home game is some other team's road game - the file
confirms it, with home wins exactly equal to road losses, and neutral-site
games landing at exactly 567-567. Two even teams, one at home, is 59.9%.
scale: fitted to the per-team quadrant records, 11,248 team-games.
staleNetWeight: before the NCAA publishes a season's first NET - around
the first Monday of December - the only full-coverage ratings are last
season's final ones, and rosters turn over. Shrinking every team toward
the average by this much pulls the forecasts toward a coin toss, which is
the honest thing to do when the ratings are a year old. It stops applying
the day the current season's NET appears.
Every team means every team, including the ones rated from the poll: the
poll line below maps onto the NET's own z scale, so a poll rating is a
reading on that scale and shrinks with it. Shrinking only the NET-rated
side would subtract two numbers measured differently, and because Kansas
is the shrunk one, it made the forecast against each ranked opponent more
confident instead of less - 21% against Oklahoma State where a consistent
shrink gives 39%.
pollFit: the AP poll is this season's information where the NET is last
season's, so a ranked team is rated from the poll instead. Points are read
as a share of the most any team could score (every ballot carries one
first-place vote, so the first-place votes count the ballots), which keeps
the mapping steady if the panel changes size. The line below was fitted to
the 2025-26 final poll against that season's final NET, 25 teams, r=0.85.
It is refitted each night once a current NET exists to fit against.
